newsitem.title: USA: Stevens eyes more asset sales, debt-easing.
newsitem.headline: Stevens eyes more asset sales, debt-easing.

text.p: Stevens International Inc said Wesnesday it was considering selling additional assets and was holding debt restructuring talks with its senior lender and noteholders.
The printing and packaging press systems manufacturer, which was hit with a $34.2 million net loss last year, said it was returning to its core business.
To reach that goal, it said it was considering additional asset sales, such as sales of its Hamilton, Hamilton Machining Center and Zerand divisions, each as a separate business unit.

The company said that proceeds from the sale of its Bernal division last month resulted in a permanent net reduction in the amount available in its senior secured debt facility to $15 million from $27 million, or 44 percent of the previous maximum available.

It said it was talking with its senior lender, Bank of America Texas, which is a BankAmerica Corp unit, and holders of its senior subordinated notes, noting that the sale of Bernal raised only modest proceeds beyond those required to repay its secured debt.

It said that while it was disappointed that it was not able to pay down its trade debt to the extent planned, it has begun to apply a portion of the proceeds to its vendors "who have been waiting in patient support of the company's restructuring plan," it said.

It said that its auditor Deloitte & Touch LLP has noted in its most recent audit that to continue as a going concern the company it must succeed in its debt restructuring, further redeploy assets and return to profitability.
Paul Stevens, chairman and chief executive officer, said that in spite of 1966 being "extremely difficult," Stevens was moving ahead with efforts to bring it back into the black.
"Accelerating the implementation of our restructuring plan...should continue to improve our productivity, increase gross margins and help Stevens return to profitability and stability," he said.
